patchouli.lucentics.name: Luxicon
patchouli.lucentics.entry.getting_starte: Welcome

Welcome once more to this lucent world.$(br2)The light of this world takes many forms, and each bears a power of its own.$(br)Yet most of that power lies beyond our command. The art of wielding it is the subject of this tome: Lucentics.

This tome does not reveal all its entries at once.$(br)As you progress, it will unveil what you need, when you need it.$(br2)Its small pages cannot record the materials and arrangements that complex rituals demand. Fortunately, $(l:https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/jei)several tools$(/l) $(l:https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/emi)have been$(/l) $(l:https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/roughly-enough-items)developed to$(/l) show the required materials and steps. Choose whichever you prefer, and let it guide your ritual.
Injector

Sunlight is the nearest of lights, yet it holds great power. Left alone, it merely warms the earth, but the right device can draw that power forth.$(br)The simplest of such devices, and the best to begin with, is the injector.

The injector gathers sunlight through the lens atop it and pours that light into the item resting on its pedestal. Certain materials with an affinity for light are transformed by it into materials of greater affinity. Begin with common materials, and observe the change.
$(br)Materials born this way are needed in every corner of Lucentics. $(o)Truly, every corner.$()$(br)Prepare several injectors beforehand, and craft a double handful of materials.
Without ample sunlight, the injection cannot proceed.
Emitter

Light by nature spreads in every direction. This suits wide illumination, but scattered light is hard to wield.$(br)The emitter gathers light within and shapes it into a single beam, loosing it through the slit at its front. Thus the power of light can be delivered to many devices.
The emitter's slit opens only while it receives a redstone signal.$(br)Light will be blocked by opaque objects, and its reach has limits.

Light loosed from an emitter flows from front to back, the near side being the front and the far side the back.$(br)This notion will prove vital when working with $(l:lucentics:prism/about_prisms#anchor1)prisms$().
Prism

Treating glass with dawnstone dust yields a mystical, translucent cube of crystal.$(br)Though called "prisms" for their appearance, they differ wholly from the objects of that name that refract and bend light.$(br)See the chapter "Prism" for details.
Daylight Level
Lucentics measures sunlight in levels from 0 to 15.$(br)This is the same value a daylight detector reads.
Color of Light

Sunlight is a fine source of light, yet alone it brings inconvenience. It is light of many colors mingled together, and no single color can be wielded apart from the rest.$(br)The tool that draws a single color from sunlight is the lens. Fitted to an $(l:lucentics:getting_started/emitter#anchor1)emitter$(), it changes the color of the light.
The materials for crafting a lens differ by color, and many seem to be items bound to the nature of that color.

Red is the color of destruction.$(br)It fells wood, cracks stone, and shatters metal. It does more than merely ruin, for it can grind things to powder, but it is poor at making anything.$(br)Its reach does not stop at objects. It may also manifest as the destruction of living things: attack.
Red Light

Blue is the color of flow.$(br)It prefers to run rather than rest, and at times it harmonizes, changing its own nature. Naturally, it has an affinity for fluids. You will be keeping its company for a long while.
Blue Light

Green is the color of creation.$(br)To make one where there was none, or to add one to what already is. It is the color best suited to crafting.$(br)Even where the matter seems less than creative, it tends to oversee whatever stands opposite destruction.
Green Light

Yellow is the color of light.$(br)Nearly everything in this world with "light" in its name falls under yellow's charge. In that sense, it may be the most important color.$(br)Lately, however, the duties of light have been shared among the other colors, and in yellow’s idle moments it is being given a new charge: energy.
Yellow Light
Magenta is the color of sorcery.$(br)Sorcery takes many forms.$(br)You will chiefly use it in brewing potions and enchanting. Yet that is not all, for it can also wield magic and spells.
Magenta Light

Cyan is the color of civilization.$(br)It governs living civilizations like villages, lost ones like ruins, and the structures that belong to them.$(br)It is also skilled at finding structures. If the one you seek cannot be found, why not take a cyan light as your guide?
Cyan Light
patchouli.lucentics.entry.devices.engrav: Properly wielded, light becomes a cutting knife that etches its mark upon things. The device that engraves new properties into materials through light rituals is this engraving table.$(br)Place the item to be worked upon the engraving table, then strike its side with light to begin the ritual.$(br)A ritual depends on the number of beams, their color, and the number and order of materials along their path.

Set a $(l:lucentics:prism/prism_ritual#anchor1)ritual prism$() upon the light’s path, and place the specified block atop it. The engraving table then links with the block above the prism, and can draw the materials the craft demands.$(br)What is etched, and how, determines the kinds and numbers of materials required, and the color of the light. Light may strike from any direction, but the order of materials along its path must match what the ritual specifies.
Engraving rituals demand great energy, so an adequate measure of sunlight must also shine upon the table.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.devices.millin: Millstones are commonly made of two parts, upper and lower, that turn against each other to grind materials into powder.$(br)This milling table is different. It spins the material instead, and the power of red light turns it to powder.$(br)Like the #engraving:engraving table$(), it is set in motion by light.
$(#aaaaaa) - I'll pulverize them all to dust
patchouli.lucentics.entry.devices.mixing: Water mingles with countless things, and is changed by them.$(br)The mixing table dissolves materials into liquid, or blends liquids together to make a new one.$(br)Like the #engraving:engraving table$(), it is set in motion by light.$(br)Compared to other devices, it has little room to hold its yield. Liquids are heavy...
$(#aaaaaa) - Since I can’t hold lots of luggage
patchouli.lucentics.entry.devices.assemb: You are skilled with your hands, and could assemble even machines by hand.$(br)Small parts are another matter, however, so leave them to the assembling table. It is a device that works the materials given to it into other materials.$(br)Like the #engraving:engraving table$(), it is set in motion by light.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.devices.pedest: The ritual pedestal holds a single kind of item. Used chiefly in ritual crafting, it marks which item the ritual calls for.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.devices.tank.t: A tank holds a set amount of a single liquid. It is also used in ritual crafting, where it marks which liquid the ritual calls for.
A variant exists with a thicker frame. The two may be converted into one another, and their basic function is the same.$(br2)To what end, one wonders?
patchouli.lucentics.entry.devices.toggle: Craft an $(l:lucentics:getting_started/emitter#anchor1)emitter$() together with a redstone torch to make a toggled emitter. Its basic function is same, but once it receives a redstone signal it keeps emitting light, and a second signal stills it again.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.devices.advanc: An $(l:lucentics:getting_started/emitter#anchor1)emitter$() strengthened with glimmer iron and a focus ring. Its light reaches twice as far, allowing more nodes to be placed along a single path.
patchouli.lucentics.category.prism.name: Prism
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.about_pr: A prism is a mystical, translucent cube of crystal.$(br)By engraving a particular symbol upon a plain prism, one may grant it a function of its own. Alone, it is but an ornament, yet it awakens when the proper light passes through it.$(br)A prism that light passes through, as well as the block at the end of the path (where the light lands), is called a "node".

Prism functions fall broadly into two kinds: "active" and "passive".$(br2)An active function remains in effect while light of the same color passes through the prism. A colorless prism responds to light of any color.$(br2)A passive function is triggered in chain with the active function of a #node:node$() #foregoing:ahead of itself$(). It takes effect even when the color of the prism and the color of the light differ.

Some prisms can transport items and liquids. What is transported becomes particles of light, travels along the path, and is drawn into the destination #node:node$(). How these particles appear is easily swayed by your $(l:https://minecraft.wiki/w/Options#Quality_&_Performance)way of seeing the world$(/l), and they may at times be seen, and at times vanish.
A valid destination is a #node:node$() that $(li)lies on the same path$()$(li)lies behind the #node:node$(/l) sending the item along the path$()$(li)is able to accept that item or liquid$().
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_ri: The ritual prism is a special prism that bears no function of its own.$(br)Instead, when a ritual of light is performed, it serves as the gateway that joins the crafting table to its inputs.$(br)The ritual prism draws its inputs from the block above it.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_im: #active:Active:$() Draws items and liquids from the container above, and carries them to a #exportable:valid destination$() on the same path.$(br2)If there is no #exportable:valid destination$(), it does nothing.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_ex: #passive:Passive: $()Accepts any items and liquids the container above can receive.$(br2)What it accepts is stored in the container above.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_io: A prism that joins the $(l:lucentics:prism/prism_importing#anchor1)importing prism$() and the $(l:lucentics:prism/prism_exporting#anchor1)exporting prism$(), and bears the nature of both.$(br)Since it sends what it receives straight on to a #exportable:valid destination$(), items and liquids may be pushed #foregoing:to the back$().
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_co: Its basic function matches the $(l:lucentics:prism/prism_io#anchor1)io prism$(), but nodes #foregoing:ahead of it$() can no longer export to the nodes beyond.$(br)That is, even if the container above this prism is full, nothing can be carried to a destination #foregoing:behind this prism$().$(br)This property proves most useful when automating rituals.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_br: #active:Active:$() Breaks the block above.$(br)Items dropped by the broken block are carried to a #exportable:valid destination$(), and whatever cannot be carried drops in place.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_at: #active:Active:$() Damages every mob within the block above.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_fl: #active:Active:$() Gathers the liquid block above as liquid and carries it to a #exportable:valid destination$(). If there is no #exportable:valid destination$(), it gathers nothing.$(br2)#passive:Passive:$() When another #node:node$() delivers an item that can hold liquid, fills that item with the liquid above. If there is a #exportable:valid destination$(), the filled item is carried there.

#passive:Passive:$() When another #node:node$() delivers an item holding liquid, draws out one bucket of the liquid and places it above. If there is a #exportable:valid destination$(), the emptied item is carried there.$(br)Likewise, when another #node:node$() delivers one bucket or more of liquid, uses one bucket of it and places it above.$(br)Neither function works unless the block above has space.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_pl: #passive:Passive:$() When another #node:node$() delivers a block item, uses one and places it above. It does not work unless the block above has space.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.prism.prism_dy: #active:Active:$() Dyes the item resting on the $(l:lucentics:devices/pedestals#anchor1)ritual pedestal$() above. Three conditions must be met.$(li)The item on the pedestal must be dyeable.$()$(li)A mixing table must lie #foregoing:behind it$(/l), holding enough dye liquid.$()$(li)A #exportable:valid destination$(/l) must lie #foregoing:further behind$(/l) the mixing table, able to receive the dyed item.$()$(br)It can carry out most dyeing recipes of an ordinary crafting table, and spends less dye in doing so.

Many prisms bear a color tied to their function. Conversely, only a plain prism of the color tied to a function may be granted that function.$(br)A plain prism cannot be dyed by ordinary dye crafting, and must instead be dyed through the dyeing prism.
Now, the dyeing prism seems itself a colored prism... Fear not. At some cost, the dyeing prism alone may be made by another path.
patchouli.lucentics.entry.material_and_t: Made by injecting light into a brick.$(br)It absorbs and releases light, and may be built up as the footing of a device.
Made by injecting light into a diorite.$(br)It scatters and deflects light, and when crushed to powder, it lets other materials attune to light.

The hammer is a tool for crushing blocks into new materials.$(br)Simple to use: place the block to be crushed, and strike it with the hammer.$(br)Some blocks must be struck more than once. The higher the hammer’s grade, the more efficient the crushing.

The golden hammer is rather peculiar. It wears down at a terrible pace, yet crushes most blocks faster than any other hammer, and yields more materials.$(br2)Hammers may also serve as a mining tool. It outperforms a pickaxe of the same kind a little, and lasts longer, but given the cost, it is not always the wiser choice.
Dye liquid is dye dissolved in water.$(br)Besides its use in rituals, it is also used in the dyeing recipes of the $(l:lucentics:prism/prism_dyeing)dyeing prism$().
Patina liquid is water in which copper dust has been dissolved and left to weather into verdigris.$(br)Used in certain rituals, it sets the dye that has been infused or applied.
